description: In place sort reorders a task list and later pushes append after it
code:
tasks = [{ name: "deploy", priority: 2 }, { name: "test", priority: 1 }, { name: "build", priority: 3 }]
tasks.sort((a, b) => a.priority - b.priority)
names = tasks.map(task => task.name)
assert(names, ["test", "deploy", "build"])
tasks.push({ name: "lint", priority: 0 })
assert(names, ["test", "deploy", "build", "lint"])
names

description: A standing sort keeps a leaderboard ordered as scores and players change
code:
class Player(name, score):
    this.name = name
    this.score = score
ana = Player("ana", 12)
ben = Player("ben", 30)
leaders = [ana, ben]
top = leaders.sort((a, b) => b.score - a.score)[0].name
assert(top, "ben")
ana.score = 45
assert(top, "ana")
assert(leaders.map(player => player.name), ["ana", "ben"])
leaders.push(Player("cy", 50))
assert(top, "cy")
top

description: Sorting a slice keeps the source order while an in place sort records a version
code:
readings = [7, 3, 9]
ordered = readings.slice().sort((a, b) => a - b)
assert(ordered, [3, 7, 9])
assert(readings, [7, 3, 9])
readings.sort((a, b) => b - a)
assert(readings, [9, 7, 3])
assert(ordered, [3, 7, 9])
assert(readings@first, [7, 3, 9])
ordered

description: Default in place sort orders numbers by their text like JavaScript
code:
codes = [10, 9, 1, 100]
codes.sort()
assert(codes, [1, 10, 100, 9])
numeric = [10, 9, 1, 100]
numeric.sort((a, b) => a - b)
assert(numeric, [1, 9, 10, 100])
codes
